claim: Starburst amacrine cells (SACs) exit the cell cycle at the apical retinal surface and migrate radially through the outer neuroblast layer (ONBL).
source: SACs exit the cell cycle at the apical retinal surface and migrate radially through the outer neuroblast layer (ONBL).

claim: SACs arrive at the inner neuroblast layer (INBL) where postmitotic neurons reside.
source: They next arrive at the inner neuroblast layer (INBL), where postmitotic neurons reside (Hinds and Hinds, 1978); Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hinds and Hinds, 1978, and reference to Figure 2A,B.

claim: SACs begin to innervate the nascent IPL, which begins to appear in some retinal regions at E16.
source: Then they begin to innervate the nascent IPL, which begins to appear in some retinal regions at E16 (Figure 2A).

Note that E16 and P1 are displayed on different scales; each plot is scaled to size of largest bin, aiding legibility in E16 plot where bin sizes are more evenly distributed. claim: A network of arbors connects somata of INBL SACs at E16.
source: (G) A network of arbors (arrows) connects somata of INBL SACs at E16.

claim: The soma-layer arbor network remains prominent in INL at P0 but is mostly gone by P2.
source: The network remains prominent in INL at P0 but is mostly gone by P2.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2G and shown in the images.

claim: Individual P1 OFF SAC INL arbors make selective contacts with SAC neighbors.

INL arbors (I) make selective contacts with SAC neighbors (purple): GFP+ arbor tips terminate on SAC somata (orange arrow) or SAC arbors (white arrows).

claim: Some P1 SACs are bi-laminar with arbors that contact neighboring somata, while others project only to IPL.
source: (J,K) Individual P1 OFF (K) and ON (L) SACs labeled by ChatmG (green) in cross-section. Purple, full SAC population. Some SACs are bi-laminar with arbors that contact neighboring somata (arrows, left panels); others project only to IPL (right panels).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2J,K and shown in the images.

claim: The frequency of soma layer projections decreases across development from P0 to P7.
source: (L) Frequency of soma layer projections across development, determined from single ChatmG cells as in J,K.
evidence: This is shown in the graph in Figure 2L.

claim: Newborn SACs establish homotypic contacts upon completion of migration and these contacts are mostly eliminated by P3.
source: (M) Schematic of newborn SAC morphology based on B-L. Soma-layer homotypic contacts are established upon completion of migration and are mostly eliminated by P3.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2M as a summary of the data shown in panels B-L.

claim: SAC dendrites form two continuous well-defined laminae by P1.
source: These markers revealed that SAC dendrites form two continuous well-defined laminae by P1 (Figure 1B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 1B,E.

claim: Some SAC dendrites were stratified already at P0, even though the P0 IPL neuropil is less than one-cell diameter wide.
source: Some dendrites were stratified already at P0, even though the P0 IPL neuropil is less than one-cell diameter wide (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: 96% of OFF SACs in the INL and 99% of ON SACs in the GCL stratified within the expected IPL sublayer at P1.
source: Further supporting this timeline, individual P1 SACs made lamina-specific projections (Figure 1C): 96% of OFF SACs in the inner nuclear layer (INL), and 99% of ON SACs in the ganglion cell layer (GCL), stratified within the expected IPL sublayer (n = 49/51 OFF; 78/79 ON; four mice).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification and sample sizes.

claim: ooDSGCs projected rudimentary and unstratified dendrites at P1.
source: By contrast, ooDSGCs projected rudimentary and unstratified dendrites at P1 (n = 18 cells, three mice, none were stratified; Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 2; also see Peng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text with sample sizes and supported by references to figures and a citation.

claim: At P2, only 30% of ooDSGCs co-fasciculated with SAC arbors; the rest projected diffusely within the IPL.
source: Even at P2, only 30% of ooDSGCs co-fasciculated with SAC arbors; the rest projected diffusely within the IPL (n = 23 cells, two mice; Figure 1D,E; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification and sample sizes, and supported by reference to figures.

claim: SACs form IPL sublayers at P0-P1, and are joined later by their synaptic partners.
source: These results indicate that SACs form IPL sublayers at P0-P1, and are joined later by their synaptic partners.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the data presented.

claim: Migrating SACs rarely interacted with each other.
source: Migrating SACs rarely interacted, but on arrival at the INBL, SAC arbors were observed touching the soma or primary dendrite of neighboring SACs (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: On arrival at the INBL, SAC arbors were observed touching the soma or primary dendrite of neighboring SACs.
source: Migrating SACs rarely interacted, but on arrival at the INBL, SAC arbors were observed touching the soma or primary dendrite of neighboring SACs (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: The majority of INBL SACs engaged in soma-layer contacts.
source: The majority of INBL SACs engaged in these soma-layer contacts, such that a GFP+ arbor network connected them (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 2G.

claim: Unlike mature SACs which exclusively project their primary dendrites toward the IPL, many E16 SACs projected tangentially through the INBL.
source: Analysis of primary dendrite orientation indicated that soma-layer contacts likely arose due to projections targeted within this layer: Unlike mature SACs, which exclusively project their primary dendrites toward the IPL, many E16 SACs projected tangentially through the INBL – that is, toward neighboring somata (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: Soma-layer SAC contact precedes IPL innervation.
source: We concluded that soma-layer SAC contact precedes IPL innervation, for three reasons.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on three lines of evidence presented in the text.

claim: Soma contacts were found in retinal regions where the IPL had not yet emerged.
source: First, soma contacts were found in retinal regions where the IPL had not yet emerged (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as the first reason supporting the conclusion that soma-layer contact precedes IPL innervation, with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Soma contacts were observed among cells that still showed migratory morphological features and did not yet project into the IPL.
source: Second, soma contacts were observed among cells that still showed migratory morphological features, such as apical and/or basal processes (Deans et al., 2011; Hinds and Hinds, 1978), and did not yet project into the IPL (Figure 2D; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as the second reason supporting the conclusion, with citations and references to figures.

claim: SAC dendrite polarization in the tangential plane was highly transient: By P1, the vast majority of SAC primary dendrites were oriented toward the IPL.
source: Third, SAC dendrite polarization in the tangential plane was highly transient: By P1, the vast majority of SAC primary dendrites were oriented toward the IPL (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is stated as the third reason supporting the conclusion, with reference to figures.

claim: At P0-1, although SAC arbors within the soma layers no longer express internexin, the arbor network remained remarkably prominent.
source: At P0-1, although SAC arbors within the soma layers no longer express internexin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), the arbor network remained remarkably prominent (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to figures.

claim: Most OFF SACs assumed a bi-laminar morphology at P0-1, with one set of arbors in the IPL and another set targeting neighboring SACs in the INL.
source: Most OFF SACs assumed a bi-laminar morphology, with one set of arbors in the IPL and another set targeting neighboring SACs in the INL (Figure 2H–J,L; Figure 2—figure supplements 2–3).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: By P2-3, the dense INL network was mostly gone.
source: By P2-3, however, this dense INL network was mostly gone (Figure 2G,L; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: ON SACs also made soma layer projections between P0 and P3 that contacted neighboring SAC somata.
source: ON SACs also made soma layer projections between P0 and P3 that contacted neighboring SAC somata (Figure 2K,L; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text with references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: Both ON and OFF SACs make transient soma-layer homotypic contacts that arise prior to IPL dendrite elaboration, and are disassembled at P2-3 after SAC sublayers have formed.
source: Together, these observations demonstrate that both ON and OFF SACs make transient soma-layer homotypic contacts that arise prior to IPL dendrite elaboration, and are disassembled at P2-3 after SAC sublayers have formed (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations presented, with reference to Figure 2M.

claim: In Six3-Cre; Ptf1aflox/flox mice, only Cre– progenitors were capable of giving rise to SACs.
source: In Six3-Cre; Ptf1aflox/flox mice (abbreviated Ptf1a-cKO), only these spared Cre– progenitors were capable of giving rise to SACs, indicating that any SACs produced in these mutants are wild-type at the Ptf1a locus (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The Ptf1a-cKO mutant creates a situation where otherwise-normal SACs are present at significantly lower density than in wild-type retina.
source: Therefore, the Ptf1a-cKO mutant creates a situation where otherwise-normal SACs are present at significantly lower density than in wild-type retina (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: In P1-2 Ptf1a-cKO mutants, some SACs were effectively segregated from their neighbors (termed 'solitary' SACs), while others had neighbors sufficiently nearby that they touched.
source: In P1-2 mutants, some SACs were effectively segregated from their neighbors – these were termed 'solitary' SACs – while others had neighbors sufficiently nearby that they touched (Figure 3B–F; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: At P1-2, touching Ptf1a-cKO SACs projected normally to the IPL, similar to SACs from Ptf1a+ littermates.
source: At P1-2, touching SACs projected normally to the IPL, similar to SACs from Ptf1a+ littermates (Figure 3D,E,G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: Solitary Ptf1a-cKO SACs largely failed to innervate the IPL.
source: By contrast, solitary SACs largely failed to innervate the IPL (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to figures.

claim: Solitary Ptf1a-cKO SACs were properly positioned at the IPL border, but sent only rudimentary arbors into it.
source: This was not caused by abnormal migration: Solitary SACs were properly positioned at the IPL border, but sent only rudimentary arbors into it (Figure 3F; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: Solitary Ptf1a-cKO SACs were more likely to project processes into the soma layers.
source: Solitary SACs were also more likely to project processes into the soma layers (Figure 3G), and when they did so, the projections were typically more elaborate than those observed in wild-type retina (Figure 3D,F; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: Both types of projection errors (IPL innervation failure and soma layer overgrowth) were also seen at P15 in Ptf1a-cKO mutants, indicating that early errors persist to retinal maturity.
source: Both types of projection errors were also seen at P15, indicating that early errors persist to retinal maturity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Homotypic interactions are specifically required for IPL innervation and sublayer formation.
source: Instead, homotypic interactions are specifically required for IPL innervation and sublayer formation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the Ptf1a-cKO data showing that generic amacrine interactions are not sufficient.

claim: MEGF10 is selectively expressed by SACs during the perinatal period.
source: First, it is selectively expressed by SACs during the perinatal period (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as the first reason MEGF10 is a candidate mediator of homotypic recognition, with references to figures.

claim: The onset of MEGF10 expression coincides with onset of SAC homotypic contact at the conclusion of radial migration.
source: Second, the onset of its expression coincides with onset of SAC homotypic contact at the conclusion of radial migration (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as the second reason MEGF10 is a candidate, with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: MEGF10 protein is present on soma-layer SAC arbors.
source: Third, MEGF10 protein is present on soma-layer SAC arbors, making it available to transduce signals arising on these arbors (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated as the third reason MEGF10 is a candidate, with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: MEGF10 mediates SAC-SAC interactions during formation of the orderly 'mosaic' among SAC cell bodies across the retina.
source: Finally, MEGF10 mediates SAC-SAC interactions in a separate context – during formation of the orderly 'mosaic' among SAC cell bodies across the retina (Kay et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as the fourth reason MEGF10 is a candidate, with a citation to Kay et al., 2012.

claim: Both ON and OFF strata were absent or severely disrupted in Megf10 null mutants at P0-1.
source: We found a striking effect on sublayer formation: Both ON and OFF strata were absent or severely disrupted in mutants (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Most Megf10–/– SACs made only rudimentary, unstratified IPL projections at P0-1.
source: These studies revealed a severe deficit in IPL dendrite arborization: Most Megf10–/– SACs made only rudimentary, unstratified IPL projections at P0-1 (n = 1/15 OFF SACs were stratified).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification.

claim: Loss of IPL innervation in Megf10 mutants was not due to aberrant SAC radial migration.
source: Loss of IPL innervation was not due to aberrant SAC radial migration, because, at P0, mutant SACs had reached the inner retina in normal numbers (wild-type, 2600 ± 287 SACs/mm2; mutant, 3153 ± 145 SACs/mm2; p=0.144, 2-tailed t-test; n = 3 each group), and were positioned adjacent to the IPL, similar to littermate controls (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification, statistical test, and reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Most mutant SACs sent at least some arbors into the IPL at P0-1.
source: Furthermore, most mutant SACs sent at least some arbors into the IPL at P0-1 (Figure 5A,C; Figure 6D), suggesting that they migrated to a location from which IPL innervation was feasible.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Mutant SAC arbors that reached the IPL appeared undifferentiated, with a lack of space-filling branches.
source: However, the mutant SAC arbors that reached the IPL appeared undifferentiated, with a lack of space-filling branches (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Mutant SAC arbors enclosed a significantly smaller IPL territory than control SACs.
source: As a result, not only did their arbors enclose a significantly smaller IPL territory, but they also failed to sample as much of their enclosed territory as control SACs (Figure 5C; also compare to control cell in Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: By P3 some ON SAC IPL innervation was evident in Megf10 mutants, but OFF SAC arbors remained largely confined to the soma layer.
source: By P3 some ON SAC IPL innervation was evident, but OFF SAC arbors remained largely confined to the soma layer; those that did reach the IPL remained undifferentiated (Figure 5B; Figure 6A,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Megf10 mutant SACs arborized exuberantly in the soma layers.
source: In contrast to their underinnervation of the IPL, Megf10 mutant SACs arborized exuberantly in the soma layers (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 6A.

claim: Both ON and OFF SACs were affected by exuberant soma layer arborization in Megf10 mutants.
source: Both ON and OFF SACs were affected (Figure 6D,E; Figure 6—figure supplement 1), but the OFF SAC phenotype was particularly striking: Starting at P1, the mutant INL network became much more elaborate than the control network of any age (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: INL arbor density increased in Megf10 mutants from P0 to P1 and remained high at P3.
source: INL arbor density increased in mutants from P0 to P1 and remained high at P3; by contrast, control SACs largely eliminated their INL projections over the same period (Figure 5A,B; Figure 6A,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: One reason for the denser mutant INL network at P2-3 was that a larger number of mutant cells projected to the soma layers.
source: From this analysis, we determined that one reason for the denser mutant network, particularly at P2-3, was that a larger number of mutant cells projected to the soma layers (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 6E.

claim: At P1, the number of cells projecting to the INL was similar in Megf10 mutants and littermate controls.
source: However, this reason was not sufficient to explain the denser mutant INL network at P1 (Figure 6C), because at that age the number of cells projecting to the INL was similar in mutants and littermate controls (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Individual mutant SACs frequently had more extensive INL arbors than littermate control SACs.
source: Supporting this conclusion, we found that mutant SACs frequently had more extensive INL arbors than littermate control SACs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 6B.

claim: Mutant SACs continued to grow primary dendrites tangentially within soma layers at P1, when the vast majority of control SACs only targeted the IPL.
source: Further, mutant SACs continued to grow primary dendrites tangentially within soma layers at P1, when the vast majority of control SACs only targeted the IPL (Figure 6F; also see Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: MEGF10 governs a developmental transition from soma-layer to IPL-layer dendrite growth.
source: Together, these data suggest that MEGF10 governs a developmental transition from soma-layer to IPL-layer dendrite growth (Figure 6G): Whereas control SACs have only a brief period of soma-layer growth, switching to IPL ramification around P0, Megf10 mutant SACs do not make this transition and instead persist in soma-layer innervation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the data presented, with reference to Figure 6G.

claim: MEGF10 is required for initial formation of SAC IPL sublayers.
source: We conclude that, because MEGF10 regulates IPL innervation in this way, MEGF10 is required for initial formation of SAC IPL sublayers.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the data presented.

claim: SACs require MEGF10 signals from their neighbors to target their dendrites properly.
source: A key prediction of this model is that SACs should require MEGF10 signals from their neighbors to target their dendrites properly.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction to be tested.

claim: In central retina of Six3-Cre; Megf10flox/lacZ animals, the vast majority of cells expressed a Cre-dependent GFP reporter, indicating that they lacked Megf10 function.
source: In central retina of Six3-Cre; Megf10flox/lacZ (Six3-Megf10-cKO) animals, the vast majority of cells expressed a Cre-dependent GFP reporter, indicating that they lacked Megf10 function (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 7A.

claim: In Six3-Megf10-cKO central retina, SACs projected exuberantly to the INL and sublayer formation was disrupted, as in null mutants.
source: Accordingly, SACs projected exuberantly to the INL and sublayer formation was disrupted, as in null mutants (Figure 7B; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: In Six3-Megf10-cKO peripheral retina, some SACs escaped Cre activity, leading to absence of the GFP reporter and continued MEGF10 protein expression.
source: In peripheral retina, some SACs escaped Cre activity, leading to absence of the GFP reporter and continued MEGF10 protein expression (Figure 7A,B; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: Megf10+ SACs surrounded by mutant SACs in Six3-Megf10-cKO retina showed a high rate of INL projections, nearly identical to their Megf10– neighbors.
source: By contrast, Megf10+ SACs surrounded by mutant SACs in Six3-Megf10-cKO retina showed a high rate of INL projections, nearly identical to their Megf10– neighbors (Figure 7B,D; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: When Megf10+ SACs are deprived of MEGF10 signal from adjacent SACs, they make exuberant soma-layer projections.
source: Thus, when Megf10+ SACs are deprived of MEGF10 signal from adjacent SACs, they make exuberant soma-layer projections. This finding implicates MEGF10 as a transcellular signal that controls SAC dendrite targeting (Figure 7K).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the Six3-Megf10-cKO data, with reference to Figure 7K.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments using intracellularly truncated Megf10 constructs showed that MEGF10 can interact with itself through its extracellular domain.
source: In support of this idea, co-immunoprecipitation experiments using intracellularly truncated Megf10 constructs showed that MEGF10 can interact with itself through its extracellular domain (Figure 7I,J; Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: MEGF10 appears biochemically capable of acting as both ligand and receptor.
source: Thus, MEGF10 appears biochemically capable of acting as both ligand and receptor.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: In Chat-Megf10-cKO animals, MEGF10 immunostaining was used to identify SACs that lost MEGF10 protein prior to P3.
source: In Chat-Megf10-cKO animals, MEGF10 immunostaining was used to identify SACs that lost MEGF10 protein prior to P3 – that is, during the period when soma-layer arbors are present (Figure 7F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: MEGF10– cells in Chat-Megf10-cKO constituted a small minority of SACs at P3, meaning that they were generally surrounded by MEGF10+ neighbors.
source: MEGF10– cells constituted a small minority of SACs at P3, meaning that they were generally surrounded by MEGF10+ neighbors (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: In Chat-Megf10-cKO, MEGF10– SACs produced more exuberant soma-layer arbors than neighboring MEGF10+ cells, while sending only minimal arbors into the IPL.
source: In this context, MEGF10– SACs produced more exuberant soma-layer arbors than neighboring MEGF10+ cells, while sending only minimal arbors into the IPL (Figure 7E–H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Single MEGF10– SACs in Chat-Megf10-cKO had phenotypes similar to SACs from mice entirely lacking Megf10.
source: Thus, single MEGF10– SACs had phenotypes similar to SACs from mice entirely lacking Megf10 (Figure 7G,H; compare to Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Adjacent MEGF10+ cells in the same Chat-Megf10-cKO retinas were indistinguishable from littermate control SACs.
source: By contrast, adjacent MEGF10+ cells in the same Chat-Megf10-cKO retinas were indistinguishable from littermate control SACs (Figure 7E,F,H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: When Megf10 is lost during dendro-somatic contact (but not after), SACs make projection errors typical of neurons deprived of homotypic interactions, even if their neighbors express MEGF10 and are developing normally.
source: Therefore, when Megf10 is lost during dendro-somatic contact (but not after; see below), SACs make projection errors typical of neurons deprived of homotypic interactions, and they do so even if their neighbors express MEGF10 and are developing normally.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the Chat-Megf10-cKO data.

claim: MEGF10 is a receptor through which SACs detect each other to terminate soma-layer growth and initiate IPL innervation.
source: Together, these experiments support the conclusion that MEGF10 is a receptor through which SACs detect each other to terminate soma-layer growth and initiate IPL innervation (Figure 7K).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the conditional mutant experiments, with reference to Figure 7K.

claim: SAC sublayers eventually formed in Megf10 mutants (by P5) and were present in the mature Megf10–/– retina, but they were marred by numerous errors.
source: We found that SAC sublayers eventually formed (by P5; Figure 8H), and were present in the mature Megf10–/– retina, but they were marred by numerous errors.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 8H.

claim: There were discontinuities in the ON and OFF strata in mature Megf10 mutants, such that mutant SACs did not completely innervate their sublaminae.
source: First, there were discontinuities in the ON and OFF strata, such that mutant SACs did not completely innervate their sublaminae (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Innervation gaps diminished retinal coverage within each mutant sublayer by ~15%.
source: These discontinuities diminished retinal coverage within each mutant sublayer by ~15% (OFF decrease, 15.0 ± 0.9%; ON decrease, 13.7 ± 4.0%; mean ±SD; n = 9 fields of view/2 mice per genotype).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification and sample sizes.

claim: Innervation gaps were not observed for other amacrine cells in Megf10 mutants, indicating that SACs were selectively affected.
source: Innervation gaps were not observed for other amacrine cells, indicating that SACs were selectively affected (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: While dendritic patterning substantially recovered between P1 and adulthood in Megf10 mutants, SAC arbor territories remained significantly smaller in mutants.
source: Examination of single SACs revealed that while dendritic patterning substantially recovered between P1 and adulthood, SAC arbor territories remained significantly smaller in mutants (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 8D.

claim: The second type of SAC error in mature Megf10–/– IPL was dendrite mistargeting to ectopic IPL strata.
source: The second type of SAC error in mature Megf10–/– IPL was dendrite mistargeting to ectopic IPL strata (Figure 8A,B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: Both ON and OFF SACs were affected by ectopic IPL projections in Megf10 mutants; in each case, ectopic arbors were mostly found in IPL regions inappropriately close to the soma layers.
source: Both ON and OFF SACs were affected; in each case, ectopic arbors were mostly found in IPL regions inappropriately close to the soma layers (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: 78.5 ± 3.5% of SACs participated in the ectopic IPL network in Megf10 mutants.
source: En-face images of mutant IPL revealed that ectopic OFF arbors formed a patchy but extensive fascicle network connecting many of the cells (Figure 8E,F; 78.5 ± 3.5% of SACs participated in the network, mean ±95% CI).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification and supported by references to figures.

claim: A soma layer-to-IPL transition occurs at P5 in Megf10 mutants, when mutant SACs began projecting to ectopic IPL locations in addition to the soma layers.
source: Supporting this view, we found that a soma layer-to-IPL transition occurs at P5, when mutant SACs began projecting to ectopic IPL locations in addition to the soma layers (Figure 8G,H; Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: This transition occurred without a significant change in the number of mutant SACs projecting into the ectopic network.
source: This transition occurred without a significant change in the number of mutant SACs projecting into the ectopic network (Figure 8F; Figure 8—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the same cells continued to participate in the network but simply altered their anatomy to target the IPL.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: Early exuberant soma-layer projections appear to give rise to adult IPL ectopias, starting between P3 and P5.
source: Thus, early exuberant soma-layer projections appear to give rise to adult IPL ectopias, starting between P3 and P5.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the developmental time course data.

claim: DS circuit sublayer formation is delayed and imperfect in the absence of MEGF10.
source: Together, these two adult mutant phenotypes demonstrate that DS circuit sublayer formation is delayed and imperfect in the absence of MEGF10.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the adult phenotype data.

claim: MEGF10 is essential for normal formation of the mature SAC IPL projection.
source: Thus, MEGF10 is essential for normal formation of the mature SAC IPL projection.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the data showing persistent errors in adult mutants.

claim: Deletion of MEGF10 prior to the onset of homotypic contact, using the Six3-Cre line, fully phenocopied Megf10–/– adult IPL errors.
source: Deletion prior to the onset of homotypic contact, using the Six3-Cre line, fully phenocopied Megf10–/– adult IPL errors (Figure 9A), suggesting a requirement for MEGF10 at the time of contact.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 9A.

claim: In Chat-Megf10-cKO mice, MEGF10 expression is largely preserved during the period when homotypic soma-layer contacts exist (prior to P3), but is eliminated shortly thereafter (between P3 and P5).
source: MEGF10 immunostaining revealed that this late, broad deletion occurs between P3 and P5 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), such that MEGF10 expression is largely preserved during the period when homotypic soma-layer contacts exist (Figure 2L), but is eliminated shortly thereafter.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: In Chat-Megf10-cKO mice, SAC laminar targeting and gap errors were exceedingly rare.
source: In this ChatCre-mediated deletion regime, SAC laminar targeting and gap errors were exceedingly rare (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 9A.

claim: Adult IPL targeting phenotypes require absence of MEGF10 during the soma-layer projection phase of SAC development – that is, prior to P3.
source: These experiments therefore define a time window for MEGF10 function (Figure 9C): Adult IPL targeting phenotypes require absence of MEGF10 during the soma-layer projection phase of SAC development – that is, prior to P3.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the conditional mutant timing experiments, with reference to Figure 9C.

claim: Any additional activity of MEGF10 after P3 is dispensable for the adult IPL phenotype.
source: Any additional activity of MEGF10 after P3 is dispensable for the adult IPL phenotype.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the Chat-Megf10-cKO data showing no IPL errors when MEGF10 is deleted after P3.

claim: The functions of MEGF10 during early homotypic contact – that is, promoting IPL innervation and terminating soma-layer arbor growth – are necessary for development of normal SAC IPL innervation at maturity.
source: These findings strongly support a model whereby the functions of MEGF10 during early homotypic contact – that is, promoting IPL innervation and terminating soma-layer arbor growth – are necessary for development of normal SAC IPL innervation at maturity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the timing experiments.

claim: In both Six3 and Chat conditional mutants, SAC positioning is less regular than in controls.
source: Mosaic spacing phenotype measured at P17 using Voronoi domain regularity index (top graph). Dashed line, index for simulated random SAC arrays. In both Six3 and Chat conditional mutants, SAC positioning is less regular than in controls (ChatCre; Megf10flox/+).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 9B and shown in the graph.

claim: Regularity effects in Megf10 conditional mutants are not due to changes in SAC cell density across genotypes.
source: Bottom graph, regularity effects are not due to changes in SAC cell density across genotypes. One-way ANOVA, F(3, 15)=0.6063; p=0.6210.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 9B and shown in the graph with statistical test.

claim: Loss of MEGF10 while soma-layer arbors are present (i.e. prior to P3) disrupts both SAC mosaic patterning and IPL laminar targeting.
source: Loss of MEGF10 while soma-layer arbors are present (i.e. prior to P3) disrupts both SAC mosaic patterning and IPL laminar targeting; this conclusion is based on phenotypes of: (1) germline mutant; (2) Six3-Megf10-cKO mutant; (3) occasional cells in Chat-Megf10-cKO mice that lost MEGF10 prior to P3 (Figure 7F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 9C as a summary of the conditional mutant results.

claim: When MEGF10 is lost after P3, as is the case for most Chat-Megf10-cKO SACs, only mosaic is disrupted.
source: When MEGF10 is lost after P3, as is the case for most Chat-Megf10-cKO SACs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), only mosaic is disrupted (A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 9C and supported by references to panels and supplementary figures.

claim: MEGF10 acts at distinct, albeit partially overlapping times, to influence SAC mosaic patterning and IPL laminar targeting.
source: Thus, MEGF10 acts at distinct, albeit partially overlapping times, to influence these two distinct SAC developmental events.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 9C as a conclusion based on the timing experiments.

claim: SAC IPL errors and mosaic spacing errors are not well correlated at the individual SAC level in Megf10 mutants.
source: Two lines of evidence suggest that this is not the case. First, the two phenotypes were not well correlated at the individual SAC level: Regardless of the severity of their mosaic spacing defects, SACs made IPL targeting errors at a constant rate (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Disturbed cell positioning does not influence the probability of making an IPL error in Megf10 mutants.
source: This finding suggests that disturbed cell positioning does not influence the probability of making an IPL error.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the lack of correlation between mosaic and IPL errors.

claim: Deletion of MEGF10 after P3 in Chat-Megf10-cKO mice caused mosaic patterning deficits, but IPL projections were largely normal.
source: Second, using our Megf10flox allele, we were able to dissociate the IPL and mosaic phenotypes: Deletion of MEGF10 after P3 in Chat-Megf10-cKO mice caused mosaic patterning deficits, but IPL projections were largely normal (Figure 9A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: IPL laminar perturbations are not an inevitable consequence of altered soma positioning in Megf10 mutants.
source: This finding demonstrates that IPL laminar perturbations are not an inevitable consequence of altered soma positioning.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the dissociation of IPL and mosaic phenotypes.

claim: Delayed IPL innervation and exuberant soma-layer arborization are likely the major sources of perturbed SAC projections at maturity in Megf10 mutants.
source: Altogether, these experiments support the notion that altered SAC position makes at best a minor contribution to IPL phenotypes; instead, delayed IPL innervation and exuberant soma-layer arborization are likely the major sources of perturbed SAC projections at maturity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the experiments dissociating mosaic and IPL phenotypes.

claim: In littermate control mice, ooDSGC dendrites were tightly and selectively associated with SAC arbors.
source: In littermate control mice (n = 9), ooDSGC dendrites were tightly and selectively associated with SAC arbors, as shown previously (Vaney and Pow, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the text with sample size and a citation.

claim: In Megf10 mutants, both normal and ectopic SAC IPL arbors reliably recruited ectopic ooDSGC projections.
source: This association was maintained in Megf10 mutants: Both normal and ectopic SAC IPL arbors reliably recruited ectopic ooDSGC projections (Figure 10A–C; Figure 10—figure supplement 1; n = 240 ectopias from five mutants,>97% contained ooDSGC arbors).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification and sample sizes, and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: When SAC gaps were present in the mutant IPL, ooDSGC dendrites typically grew around the gap edges and failed to enter them.
source: Further, when SAC gaps were present in the mutant IPL, ooDSGC dendrites typically grew around the gap edges and failed to enter them (Figure 10D; Figure 10—figure supplement 1; n = 325 gaps from five mutants, >95% devoid of ooDSGC arbors).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification and sample sizes, and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: SACs provide both permissive cues required for ooDSGC IPL innervation, and also attractive cues sufficient to recruit ooDSGCs to the wrong IPL sublayer.
source: Thus, SACs provide both permissive cues required for ooDSGC IPL innervation, and also attractive cues sufficient to recruit ooDSGCs to the wrong IPL sublayer.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the ooDSGC phenotypes in Megf10 mutants.

claim: In wild-type retina, DS-circuit bipolar cells arborized in close contact with SAC dendrites; however, unlike ooDSGCs, they remained adjacent to SACs rather than overlapping them.
source: In wild-type retina, DS-circuit bipolar cells arborized in close contact with SAC dendrites; however, unlike ooDSGCs, they remained adjacent to SACs rather than overlapping them (Figure 11A–D; Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: In Megf10 mutants, axons of all four DS-circuit bipolar cell types were recruited to ectopic IPL locations by mistargeted SAC arbors, where they stratified adjacent to SACs.
source: This arrangement was preserved in Megf10 mutants: Axons of all four bipolar cell types were recruited to ectopic IPL locations by mistargeted SAC arbors, where they stratified adjacent to SACs (Figure 11B–D,F; Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures and supplementary figures.

claim: BC5 and BC7 terminals always sandwiched SAC arbors in Megf10 mutants, regardless of their IPL location.
source: For example, BC5 and BC7 terminals always sandwiched SAC arbors, regardless of their IPL location – even when doing so required formation of a supernumerary BC axon field between the normal and ectopic SAC sublayers (Figure 11C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: SAC arbor clumps shifted BC7 terminals significantly toward the GCL by ~4 µm in Megf10 mutants.
source: Their arbors were pushed farther apart by SAC arbor clumps (Figure 11C–E), which shifted BC7 terminals significantly toward the GCL by ~4 µm (69 ± 0.8% of IPL depth in control regions to 74 ± 1.9% in affected regions; mean ± S.E.M.; n = 21 control, n = 6 affected; 2-tailed t-test, p=0.0024).
evidence: This is stated in the text with specific quantification, sample sizes, and statistical test, and supported by references to figures.

claim: DS-circuit bipolar cell projections were minimally affected by SAC IPL gaps in Megf10 mutants.
source: However, in contrast to ooDSGCs, bipolar cell projections were minimally affected by SAC IPL gaps. While BC5 and BC7 terminals were slightly mispositioned in the absence of SAC arbors – they were closer together – innervation of gap regions was otherwise normal (Figure 11C–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: DS-circuit bipolar axons either do not require SAC-derived signals for IPL innervation, or the relevant signals are capable of acting over larger distances than the typical SAC IPL gap size.
source: Thus, DS-circuit bipolar axons either do not require SAC-derived signals for IPL innervation, or the relevant signals are capable of acting over larger distances than the typical SAC IPL gap size (35–45 µm maximum diameter).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the bipolar cell gap phenotype.

claim: Early-stratifying SACs form a scaffold that directs IPL laminar targeting of their circuit partners using multiple guidance strategies.
source: Altogether, these analyses of DS circuit anatomy in Megf10 mutants support the notion that early-stratifying SACs form a scaffold that directs IPL laminar targeting of their circuit partners using multiple guidance strategies.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the analysis of circuit partner phenotypes in Megf10 mutants.

claim: Impairment of SAC interactions in the perinatal retina causes permanent functional DS circuit deficits.
source: We found that impairment of SAC interactions in the perinatal retina causes permanent functional DS circuit deficits.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the physiological recordings from Megf10 mutants.

claim: In Megf10 mutants, direction tuning of ooDSGCs becomes broader and weaker.
source: In Megf10 mutants, direction tuning of ooDSGCs becomes broader and weaker, and their ON/OFF preferred directions are less aligned.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a summary of the physiological findings.

claim: Direction tuning is degraded in Megf10 mutants in large part because mutant ooDSGCs have aberrant spiking responses to null-direction stimuli.
source: Direction tuning is degraded in large part because mutant ooDSGCs have aberrant spiking responses to null-direction stimuli.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an explanation for the broader and weaker tuning.

claim: Impaired null-direction inhibition – which arises from SACs – is a key contributor to the physiological phenotype in Megf10 mutants.
source: This suggests that impaired null-direction inhibition – which arises from SACs – is a key contributor to the phenotype.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the increased null-direction spiking.

claim: Broader ooDSGC tuning curves degrade population-level coding of directional information, and the ability of downstream neurons to extract such information.
source: Broader ooDSGC tuning curves have been shown, in modeling studies, to degrade population-level coding of directional information, and the ability of downstream neurons to extract such information (Fiscella et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to a modeling study.

claim: The physiological phenotypes identified in Megf10 mutants are likely sufficient to impair the ability of mutant retina to appropriately relay visual information.
source: Thus, the physiological phenotypes we identified are likely sufficient to impair the ability of mutant retina to appropriately relay visual information.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the physiological findings and modeling studies.

claim: Dysfunctional DS circuit physiology in Megf10 mutants is almost certainly a consequence of its effects on development, because neurons do not express MEGF10 beyond the second postnatal week.
source: Dysfunctional DS circuit physiology in Megf10 mutants is almost certainly a consequence of its effects on development, because neurons do not express MEGF10 beyond the second postnatal week (Kay et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: Anatomical changes to the DS circuit arising during development are responsible for circuit dysfunction in Megf10 mutants.
source: We therefore conclude that anatomical changes to the DS circuit arising during development are responsible for circuit dysfunction.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the lack of MEGF10 expression in adult neurons and lack of Müller glia changes.

claim: The fundamental change to DS circuit anatomy in Megf10 mutants is altered distribution of arbors and synapses.
source: The fundamental change to DS circuit anatomy in Megf10 mutants is altered distribution of arbors and synapses, unlike other manipulations which simply serve to destroy SAC radial morphology or disrupt synaptic partnering among DS circuit cells (Sun et al., 2013; Duan et al., 2014; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Peng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to other studies for comparison.

claim: In Megf10 mutants, the combined effect of mosaic spacing defects and IPL laminar targeting errors is to disturb the regularity of SAC IPL innervation.
source: In Megf10 mutants, the combined effect of mosaic spacing defects and IPL laminar targeting errors is to disturb the regularity of SAC IPL innervation.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a summary of the anatomical changes.

claim: Some parts of the visual map become over-innervated while others are uninnervated in Megf10 mutants.
source: As a result, some parts of the visual map become over-innervated (e.g. Figure 10C) while others are uninnervated (Figure 10D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by references to figures.

claim: ooDSGCs are recruited to the over-innervated regions and excluded from uninnervated gaps in Megf10 mutants, likely causing sporadic local inhomogeneity in synapse density across visual space.
source: In turn, ooDSGCs are recruited to the over-innervated regions and excluded from uninnervated gaps, likely causing sporadic local inhomogeneity in synapse density across visual space.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an interpretation of the ooDSGC recruitment and exclusion patterns.

claim: The finding that Megf10 mutants have DS tuning phenotypes suggests that local synaptic arrangements are important for the DS computation.
source: The finding that Megf10 mutants have DS tuning phenotypes suggests that local synaptic arrangements are indeed important for the DS computation.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the physiological findings in the context of different models of DS.

claim: The developmental mechanisms described in this study are important for enabling circuit function.
source: More broadly, this finding shows that the developmental mechanisms we describe here are important for enabling circuit function, raising the possibility that other circuits throughout the retina and CNS may use similar developmental mechanisms to establish their functional connectivity.
evidence: This is stated as a broader conclusion based on the findings.
